title: Check the loop actually builds most of its day now
goal: A day after the walk sweep was put on a schedule, look at where the loop actually spent its time and say whether the change worked. If it did not, the schedule needs another turn of the knob rather than another guess.
notes:
Before the change, measured 2026-09-21T15:41Z over 24h: tasks 597m (41.4%), sweeps 834m (57.9%), between 9m (0.6%), 13 full-set runs, 8 tasks. Over 48h: tasks 36.2%, sweeps 63.0%, 28 full-set runs.

The projection in queue/audits/2026-09-21-sweep-schedule.json is 21 to 27 per cent on walk checks. The knob is PHOTONZ_SWEEP_FLOOR_HOURS (default 12, queue/bin/sweep-schedule.mjs) and PHOTONZ_SLICE_MINUTES (default 10).

If the share is still bad, the two likeliest causes are the rotating check costing more than budgeted (a cold probe build is minutes, and it is not in the ten minute budget) and the full sweep having grown past 113 minutes.
acceptance: queue/bin/loop-day.mjs --hours 24 is run on or after 2026-09-22 and its numbers are written into this task
The share of the day spent on tasks is over 50 per cent, or the task says what is eating it instead
The number of full sweeps in that day is 2 or fewer, and the number of rotating checks is written down

log.note: MEASURED 2026-09-22T12:13Z by the digest pass. node queue/bin/loop-day.mjs --hours 24: tasks 828m 57.5% over 20 tasks, sweeps 410m 28.4% over 5 full-set runs, slices 175m 12.1% over 16 rotating checks, between 28m 1.9%. Over 48h: tasks 51.9%, sweeps 40.7%, slices 6.1%. Against 2026-09-21's 41.4% tasks and 57.9% sweeps, the knob worked: building is the majority of the day for the first time. Acceptance item 2 is met. Acceptance item 3 is NOT: 5 full-set runs in the window against a ceiling of 2, and the rotating checks are written down above.

WHY the count is 5 and what is left to fix. The floor landed at 2026-09-21T16:01Z, so only three of those five are its responsibility: runs beginning 2026-09-22T01:47Z, 08:30Z and 10:12Z. The 10:12Z one is CORRECT and deliberate: the 08:30Z run went blind, and sweep-record.mjs (line 88 onward) keeps a blind run out of latest.json on purpose so it 'does not buy itself half a day of nobody looking again'. The 01:47Z one is correct too: queue/loop.log shows a clean ramp of rotating checks reporting 2.9h, 3.9h ... 9.9h before it, so the twelve hours really had passed. The ONE that is unexplained is 08:30Z (01:30 local, queue/loop.log line 246605). Twenty two minutes before it the slice at 01:08 local correctly said '6.4h since the last whole-set run'. Handing sweep-schedule.mjs decide() those same inputs by hand returns {run: slice, why: 6.7h since the last whole-set run}, and none of the eight requests that run served carries now:true, so it was not a --now jump. What else happened in those twenty two minutes: commit 40bbb38c, the blind-sweep change, landed and rewrote sweep-record.mjs. Start there: can that change move an already-recorded run out of latest.json, or leave latest.json unreadable, so the next decision measures from a much older run and every sweep after it is due immediately? That is the whole remaining cost, about two hours of the day.

MEASURED 2026-09-23T02:27Z. node queue/bin/loop-day.mjs --hours 24 (window 2026-09-22T02:27Z to 2026-09-23T02:27Z): tasks 861m 59.8% over 24 tasks, sweeps 320m 22.2% over 3 full-set runs, slices 229m 15.9% over 21 rotating checks, between 30m 2.1%. Against 2026-09-21's 41.4% building and 57.9% sweeping, and against yesterday's 57.5%. Acceptance 1 and 2 are met: building is the majority of the day and still climbing. Acceptance 3 is met on the rotating-check half (21, written down) and NOT on the sweep count: 3 full-set runs against a ceiling of 2.

CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, and it is the same 08:30Z run yesterday's pass could not explain. It was never the schedule's arithmetic. queue/loop.log lines 246594-246605: the task a-sweep-that-goes-blind-says-so-instead-of-faili exited 0 at 01:30:48 local and the loop started a full sweep SEVEN SECONDS later, twenty two minutes after a rotating check had correctly printed '6.4h since the last whole-set run'. That runner had repaired a poisoned latest.json by replaying the whole-set run of 2026-09-21T06:47:03Z through recordSweep() by hand (loop.log 246512-246514: 'cp queue/sweep/latest.json /tmp/latest-poisoned-backup.json', then recordSweep, then 'git log --until=2026-09-21T06:47:03Z'). It was right about the walks and it moved latest.began back nineteen hours. sweep-schedule.mjs counts its twelve hour floor from that same field, so the floor collapsed.

REPRODUCED before and after, by replaying that exact repair against a temp sweep dir with latest.json as it stood at 01:47Z. Before (git show HEAD:queue/bin/sweep-record.mjs): '-> latest.began is now: 2026-09-21T06:47:03Z' and decide() at 2026-09-22T08:30:55Z returns 'full: 25.7h since the last whole-set run', which is the line the loop acted on. After: '==> This run ended 2026-09-21T08:39:00Z, which is NOT after the run already recorded, so it is not written over it...', began stays 2026-09-22T01:47:41Z, and decide() returns 'nothing'.

THE FIX, three parts. (1) queue/bin/sweep-record.mjs: latest.json only ever moves forward. The newer-than check was an opt-in parameter (onlyIfNewer) that only sweep-recover.mjs passed, and the hand-repair path is exactly the one that did not; it is now unconditional and the parameter is gone. The CLI says so when it refuses, and names deleting latest.json as the way to mean it. (2) queue/bin/go-loop.sh: the full-sweep line now prints the reason, via a new 'sweep.sh why' verb, so it reads 'walk sweep due (20.5h since the last whole-set run)'. Until now it said only 'due', which is why this took two passes to find: a sweep on a collapsed floor looked identical to one on a full twelve hours. (3) queue/bin/digest-prompt.md: the daily digest now ends its Summary with loop-day.mjs numbers and calls out a third full sweep or a blind run, so the share self-measures instead of needing a task to check it.

VERIFIED. New drill scenario 4b in queue/bin/sweep-interrupt-drill.mjs (already in CI, .github/workflows/ci.yml line 51) proves a complete older run is refused with no flag passed, that began does not move, and closes the loop to the cost: decide() says not-due with the record left alone and 'full' with it moved back. All drills green: sweep-interrupt, sweep-parse, sweep-notes, sweep-line, sweep-schedule, sweep-blind, loop-day, sweep-size. sweep.sh and go-loop.sh checked with the interpreters on their own shebang lines (bash and zsh respectively), and the new line rendered end to end against a fake sweep dir.

WHAT THE THIRD SWEEP COST, and what is left. The three runs were 08:30Z (blind, 79m, thrown away), 10:12Z (118m) and 22:56Z (122m). Only 08:30Z was wrong; 10:12Z follows from it deliberately, because a blind run is kept out of latest.json on purpose so it does not buy itself half a day of nobody looking. So the backwards write cost about 3.3 hours of the day, and with it gone the window should hold 2 full sweeps. Acceptance 3 is now fixed at its cause rather than verified in a clean window, and the digest line is what verifies it from tomorrow on without another task.

left rough: a blind run still costs the day twice, 79 minutes thrown away plus a 118 minute re-run 1.7h later. That is the deliberate trade made on 2026-09-22 (a blind run must not buy half a day of nobody looking) and it is the right call while blindness is rare, so it is not filed. If blind runs stop being rare the answer is to make the re-run resume from where the probe died rather than restart the set.

The schedule worked and the one sweep that should not have run is fixed at its cause. Measured 2026-09-23T02:27Z with loop-day.mjs --hours 24: tasks 861m 59.8% over 24 tasks, sweeps 320m 22.2% over 3 full-set runs, slices 229m 15.9% over 21 rotating checks, between 30m 2.1%, against 41.4% building and 57.9% sweeping the day before the floor landed. Acceptance 1 and 2 met. Acceptance 3 met on the rotating checks (21, written down) and not on the sweep count, so I chased the extra one: the blind-sweep runner had repaired a poisoned latest.json by replaying a nineteen-hour-old whole-set run through recordSweep() by hand, and the schedule counts its twelve hour floor from that same began field, so the floor collapsed and the loop started a full sweep seven seconds after that task ended. Reproduced before and after (before: decide() says 'full: 25.7h since the last whole-set run'; after: 'nothing'). Fixed in 6274ee44: latest.json only ever moves forward whoever is writing, the loop's log now prints why a full sweep is due instead of just 'due', and the daily digest reports where the day went so the share self-measures. New scenario in sweep-interrupt-drill.mjs (already in CI) proves both the refusal and the cost it stops. All sweep drills green, Scripts/test.sh green (9105 tests, 726 suites). No audit: this is loop infrastructure, nothing in the app became playtestable. No sweep requested, since nothing under Sources/ or Scripts/playtest was touched.
